pois.name: Endurance: main hull
pois.note: Published position 68°44′21″S 52°19′47″W (Wikipedia "Endurance (1912 ship)", matching the FMHT-sourced 3,008 m depth). This tile's terrain here reads 3,000.3 m, 7.7 m shallower than the published 3,008 m -- close agreement for a smooth GEBCO-derived fill (see sources.md). depth_m sits ~5 m above the seabed for a scan target at roughly deck height on the intact, upright hull.

pois.name: Stern: "ENDURANCE" and the pole star
pois.note: The ship's name is visible on the stern "directly below the taffrail" (FMHT), above a five-pointed star that stood for her original name Polaris (History.com). Placed 20 m from endurance-hull's centre, toward the assumed stern; no source publishes the ship's exact heading (see sources.md), so this offset is illustrative, not surveyed.

pois.name: The ship's wheel
pois.note: Endurance22 photographed "the helm of the Endurance" (History.com) and a large white anemone near the wheel, among sea stars, sponges and sea squirts colonising the hull (Smithsonian, quoting BAS marine biogeographer Huw Griffiths). Placed near the stern, illustrative position (no coordinate published for the wheel itself).

pois.name: Fallen masts and funnel
pois.note: FMHT's survey team (Mensun Bound) found the masts down and the funnel toppled, with damage concentrated around the poop and waist; History.com's photo set shows the ship appears to have struck the seabed bow/keel-first. No coordinates are published for the fallen rigging itself; placed forward of the hull centre, illustrative position.
